text:
Maya S.: Heads-up — seeing quota enforcement gaps on prod. model-specific throttles for the `m-prod-*` family didn't trigger and a few orgs burned through burst credits. anyone oncall? @Kevin L.?
InfraBot: ALERT: quota_service.report: org=acme-corp event=overrun tokens_dropped=120384 models=[m-prod-7b,m-prod-3b]
Kevin L.: I can grab it. quick question: where are we currently checking model-specific quotas — gateway layer or at runtime?
Oliver P.: right now gateway enforces per-key org quotas, runtime applies generic token limits. model-specific rules only live in the quota_service DB but enforcement path is flaky during fallback routing.
Sophie R.: this is why we discussed moving enforcement earlier in the request path (pre-routing) so we don't let requests route to incompatible variants and blow burst buckets.
Maya S.: agree. For this incident root cause: router fell back to m-prod-7b from m-prod-3b during capacity crunch; weight accounting used org-token-count (not model-weighted) so 7b consumed same tokens as 3b.
Zara K.: can we adopt a weight multiplier per family? e.g., big models count as 4 units, small as 1. that would make quota math reflect real cost.
Kevin L.: that's sensible. two implementation concerns: (1) where to store/serve weights (catalog vs quota_service cache) and (2) rate-limit header explosion if we include per-model details in HTTP response.
Sophie R.: UX asks: console needs a per-model-family panel showing: committed quota, burst_remaining, effective_weight, and a timeline of rejects. shadow/enforce toggle would help canary rollout.
Oliver P.: proposal: enforcement point stays at gateway but gateway consults quota_service which returns either {allow, deny, shadow, adjusted_tokens}. Gateway applies adjusted_tokens = tokens * weight and decrements bucket atomically.
Kevin L.: atomics are tricky cross-region. maybe return a reservation token from quota_service: `reserve( org, model_family, tokens ) -> reservation_id` then gateway emits request with reservation_id to runtime. If quota_service is down, fallback policy = conservative deny.
Maya S.: agree reservation pattern is safer. Also telemetry: we need per-org_per-model counters for token_burn, rejected_count, shadow_hits. add 1% sampling to full request traces until we see stable metrics.
Sophie R.: for headers I suggest a small summary: `X-RW-Quota: profile=family-A;rem=12000;weight=4` and full breakdown via GET /v1/quotas?org=... (console consumes that). avoids giant headers.
Kevin L.: alternate: `X-RW-Quota-Profile: id=fp-1323` then client can call /v1/quota-profiles/fp-1323 if needed. avoids exposing internals to clients.
Zara K.: how do we migrate existing customers? default weight=1 unless they opt-in. plan a 2-week shadow period where we compute adjusted_burn in telemetry but don't enforce.
Oliver P.: metrics to add: `model.family.token_rate`, `model.family.rejected`, `model.family.shadow_ratio`, and `quota.reservations.failed`. dashboards + alert on rejected increase > 3x baseline.
Maya S.: rollout steps I propose: 1) proto API for reservation + header schema 2) quota_service weight table + admin UI 3) gateway + runtime changes in canary with shadow mode 4) enable enforcement per-org by flag 5) full rollout + doc and SDK updates.
Kevin L.: SDK note: we'll expose `quota_profile_id` in response object. languages should ignore unknown fields to remain compatible.
Sophie R.: mockups: I'll drop a console panel PNG in #product-design by EOD. Panel will let SREs set family weight, burst window, and toggle shadow/enforce.
InfraBot: DEPLOYMENT: canary rollout of quota-service v2 started (deploy-bot).
Maya S.: Action items: @Kevin L. spec reservation API + failure modes (due EOD Thu), @Oliver P. telemetry metrics PR + dashboard skeleton, @Sophie R. console mockup + admin endpoints, @Zara K. create migration plan for default weights.
Kevin L.: I started a doc: https://redwood.internal/notes/model-quota-reservation (WIP). putting notes on cross-region reservations and idempotency.
Zara K.: thumbs up. I'll draft migration playbook and hold office hours with a couple big customers.
Maya S.: thanks all — let's keep this thread for coord. will escalate to incidents channel if we need paging. :white_check_mark:
